_about: Public-domain William Fleetwood (1656-1723), Bishop of St Asaph and then of Ely, for the Word Hoard: A Compleat Collection of the Sermons, Tracts and Pieces (1737), The Relative Duties of Parents and Children, Husbands and Wives, Masters and Servants, The Reasonable Communicant, An Essay upon Miracles, Seventeen Sermons, Four Sermons, A Sermon upon Swearing, and a sermon on the education of children. His anonymous pieces (the Life of the Blessed Virgin, the Romans XIII vindication, the lay-baptism tract, the Defence of Praying before Sermon, the Life of St Wenefrede, the Curate of Wilts letter) are held until Adam rules on catalogue attributions. Texts are from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-24 by lane A, round 137 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

fleetwood-compleat-collection: A compleat collection of the sermons, tracts, and pieces of all kinds, that were written by the Right Reverend Dr. William Fleetwood, ...  1737 (catalogued 1737)
fleetwood-relative-duties: The relative duties of parents and children, husbands and wives, masters and servants, consider'd in sixteen sermons: with three more upon the case of self-murther. By W. Fleetwood, ...  1705 (catalogued 1705)
fleetwood-reasonable-communicant: The reasonable communicant: or, an explanation of the doctrine of the Sacrament of the Lord's-Supper, in all its parts, from the communion-service. In a discourse between a minister and one of his parishioners.  1704 (catalogued 1704)
fleetwood-miracles: An essay upon miracles. In two discourses. By William Fleetwood, ...  1701 (catalogued 1701)
fleetwood-seventeen-sermons: Seventeen sermons preach'd upon several occasions. By W. Fleetwood, ... First collected together.  1717 (catalogued 1717)
fleetwood-four-sermons: Four sermons: I. On the death of Queen Mary, 1694. II. On the death of the Duke of Gloucester, 1700. III. On the death of King William, 1701. IV. On the Queen's accession to the throne, in 1703. By William Lord Bishop of St. Asaph.  1712 (catalogued 1712)
fleetwood-swearing: A sermon upon swearing. Preached at his parish. By William, late Lord Bishop of S. Asaph.  1721 (catalogued 1721)
fleetwood-education-children: A sermon of the education of children,...  1696 (catalogued 1696)

_excluded.fleetwood-single-sermons: his separately printed sermons of 1689 to 1718 are gathered in the 1737 Compleat Collection, so they are not shelved one by one
_excluded.fleetwood-secular: Chronicon Preciosum, the wheat-price account and the Latin Inscriptionum Antiquarum Sylloge are not theology
_excluded.fleetwood-political: Revolution Principles and Papists not Excluded from the Throne are political
_excluded.fleetwood-dups: later printings of the Relative Duties, the Reasonable Communicant, the Romans vindication and the swearing sermon, and the 1736 proposals
_excluded.fleetwood-anonymous: the Curate of Wilts letters, the Holborn letter, the funeral sermon upon Mr Noble 'by a neighbouring minister' and The Perfectionists Examin'd are not signed
